tagline: JCI‑accredited regional eye‑care hub with cornea & vitreo‑retina services

description: Ahalia Foundation Eye Hospital (AFEH) is the flagship ophthalmology centre of the Ahalia Health, Heritage & Knowledge Village at the Ahalia Campus, Kozhippara, Palakkad. The group presents itself as a JCI‑accredited eye hospital and operates a large network of regional centres across Kerala.

The hospital runs subspecialty services — vitreo‑retina, cornea and corneal transplantation (eye bank), glaucoma, paediatric ophthalmology, oculoplasty and low‑vision rehabilitation — and supports training programmes (DNB/FNB/DO and fellowships).

AFEH is backed by an in‑campus diagnostic facility (Ahalia Central Laboratory) that is presented online as NABL‑accredited, and the group is empanelled on several state/national schemes and insurer lists for regional access and cashless care.

For patients in Palakkad district the hospital functions as a referral centre for complex retinal and corneal surgery while maintaining a network of regional clinics for follow‑up and community ophthalmology outreach.
highlights: JCI‑listed eye hospital and Kerala‑wide regional network.
Vitreo‑retina clinic and full vitreoretinal surgical capability.
Cornea services with eye bank and corneal transplantation.
On‑site NABL‑accredited central laboratory supporting diagnostics.
Training programmes: DNB/FNB/DO and vitreo‑retina fellowship.

sections.heading: Background
body: AFEH is the ophthalmology flagship within the Ahalia Health, Heritage & Knowledge Village (Ahalia Campus, Kozhippara). The group describes the eye hospital as JCI‑accredited and highlights a broad network of regional centres across Kerala, making advanced eye care accessible to the region.

sections.heading: Services and subspecialities
body: The hospital lists comprehensive ophthalmology services: cataract and phaco, refractive surgery (LASIK), glaucoma, pediatric ophthalmology and squint, orbit and oculoplasty, uvea clinic, low‑vision rehabilitation and prosthetic eye services. Subspecialty emphasis includes vitreo‑retina (medical and surgical) and cornea services with an eye bank and corneal transplantation programme.

Diagnostics and theatre support cited on the hospital site and brochure include OCT, fundus cameras, phaco systems, YAG/green lasers, Humphrey visual field analysers and microsurgical instruments required for retina and corneal work. The campus also promotes in‑house training (DNB/FNB/fellowships) that supports its subspecialty teams.

sections.heading: Plan your visit
body: Make an appointment for subspecialty clinics (retina / cornea) — these clinics often run by appointment and may require prior referral or diagnostic reports. Confirm subspecialty surgeon availability before travel.

Check insurance/empanelment and cashless scheme status (PM‑JAY / state empanelment or private insurers) before admission. For urgent retinal emergencies attend the main campus (Ahalia Campus, Kozhippara) and call the hospital contact numbers to alert the team.

latest.text: Ahalia's official 2026 brochure (AHHKV NEW BROCHURE) published May 4, 2026 restates the campus services and lists Ahalia Foundation Eye Hospital's vitreo‑retina, cornea (eye bank/corneal transplant) and the statewide regional centre network.

visitorInfo.bestTime: Year‑round; outpatient clinics run weekdays — book appointments for subspecialty visits and urgent retina work any time.
visitorInfo.howToReach: Ahalia Campus (Kozhippara, Palakkad) is reached by road from Palakkad town (KSRTC and private taxis); the nearest major railhead is Palakkad Junction and regional buses/ taxis serve Kozhippara/Ahalia campus — confirm local connections and book intercity transport before travel.
etiquette: Call ahead for retina or cornea appointments and bring prior scans (OCT/fundus photos) or referral notes.
Confirm insurance/PM‑JAY/empanelment and pre‑authorisation before elective admission.
If travelling for corneal transplant or vitreoretinal surgery, arrange local accommodation near Ahalia Campus for post‑op follow‑ups.
For eye‑donation or eye bank queries contact the hospital’s eye bank team — consent and documentation are required.
